An introduction ·
The system in one page
This system answers three questions. Everything else follows from them.
Question · 01
What makes Sharnay visually recognizable — beyond the logo?
A restrained visual signature. The aperture DNA, a mono-caption archival voice, a three-voice type system, and editorial rhythm — image, caption, negative space. Someone can recognize a Sharnay page without ever seeing the wordmark.
Ch. I · Light  ·  Ch. IV · Perspective
Question · 02
How does that language come directly from the craft?
Six words, native to photography. Light. Frame. Focus. Perspective. Depth. Print. Every chapter, every icon, every editorial device descends from these — the vocabulary photographers already understand.
Ch. II · Frame  ·  Ch. III · Focus
Question · 03
What does it look like — applied to Erika's actual business?
An Instagram that reads as a curated exhibition. Print applications that feel meant-to-be-held. A grid, a business card, a print box — one system, moving from screen to hand without breaking voice.
Ch. VI · Print  ·  Ch. VII · Surface

I Chapter One · Light Deliverable 01 · Signature Symbol System 01 / 09
I

Everything begins
with light.

The aperture is where light enters the camera. It is also the point where our visual language begins. Every mark in this system descends from a single geometry — six blades, meeting in a circle, opening to the world.

The master mark.

One shape, five expressions. The aperture appears at every scale and finish — from a favicon that reads at 16 pixels to a foil stamp pressed into archival paper. It is never redrawn. Only reinterpreted.

01Primary
02Reversed
03Solid
04Foil Stamp
05Favicon · 32px
01·07 · Lockups
Three forms. Only two of them are the logo.

The symbol on its own is the logomark. The logo is the logomark with the words, and it exists in two arrangements: side by side, and stacked. Each form has a shape it wants to be, and a box it must never be forced into.

01·07 Linear lockup · 3.44 : 1
01·08 Logomark · 1 : 1
01·09 Stacked lockup · 0.91 : 1
01·10 · Construction
Every gap is a fraction of the mark.

Nothing in a lockup is set in absolute units. The height of the logomark is the unit, written M below, and every other measure follows from it. That is why both arrangements survive any scale without being re-measured.

Linear · gap
0.11 M
The words sit at the same height as the mark and share its baseline.
Linear · words
2.37 M
Width of the wordmark, measured off the master artwork.
Stacked · mark
1.35 M
The mark grows when stacked, because it has the full width to hold.
Stacked · gap
0.16 M
A vertical join needs more air than a horizontal one to read as one object.
01·10 None of these figures is an opinion. Each was measured off the master artwork, and the two linear files that were circulating separately agreed on every one of them to within one percent. Measured
01·11 · Limits
Air, floor, and two colours.

Clear space is one logomark height on every side. The floors are not preferences either: they come from the thinnest stroke in the artwork, at the size where that stroke falls below a single pixel and the form begins to break. Gold is a finish, not a colour state.

Clear space
1.0 M
All four sides, all three forms, no exception for tight layouts.
Logomark floor
34 px
Below this the vector is rebuilt at a heavier stroke, as the favicon does at 32.
Linear floor
51 px
Height. The words set this limit, not the mark.
Stacked floor
131 px
Height. The words occupy 0.39 of the block, so the block must be taller.
Logomark goes
Tight chrome
Fixed rails, favicon, stickers, watermark. Anywhere a bar is shorter than 100px.
Linear goes
Wide and calm
Letterhead, email, web footer, certificate. It needs 153px of vertical room to keep its clear space.
Stacked goes
Square and tall
Avatars, covers, packaging, any format that is not wider than it is tall.
Never
Force a fit
If a form does not fit its space with air, the answer is another form, not a smaller one.
01·11 Never rebuild a lockup from its parts. Never change a gap. Never stretch. Never put the linear lockup in a square box: that single error emptied the canvas and pushed the mark off centre in five places at once. Forbidden

Construction.

The aperture is built on a 12-column optical grid. Six blades meet at the circle's center at 60° increments. Never scaled by percentage — only rebuilt.

12 × 12 Grid · Ø 100
6 Blades · 60° Rotation

II Chapter Two · Frame Deliverable 03 · Editorial Graphic Elements 02 / 09
II

A frame is a
decision.

What we include is not more important than what we leave out. The editorial devices below are the tools of that decision — the crop, the corner, the registration mark. Never decorative. Always functional.

The tools of the decision.

The vocabulary of the darkroom, the contact sheet, and the print shop — translated into a modern editorial system. Each device carries meaning: orientation, sequence, authenticity. Each appears only when it serves the page.

III Chapter Three · Focus Deliverable 02 · Custom Icon Family 03 / 09
III

Focus is
the act of choosing.

Twelve icons, one family. Six are built explicitly on the aperture's six-blade geometry. Six share only its stroke, corner, and grid — the family resemblance without the literal shape. Erika chooses which rule the system follows.

A · Explicit aperture geometry06 marks

Every icon incorporates the aperture's hexagonal blade construction. The DNA is literal and readable at every scale.

B · Implicit shared DNA06 marks

Same stroke weight, same corner radius, same optical grid — but the aperture appears only as the master mark. Restrained. Editorial.

Construction rules.

Regardless of family, every icon obeys the same physical grammar. This is what makes the system unmistakable — not the individual mark, but the consistency between marks.

Optical grid
24 px
Fixed. All variants scale from 24.

1.25 pt
Digital. 0.5pt for print.
Corner
Round
Line-cap & line-join.

None
Outline system. Never filled.
Blade angle
60°
Aperture derived. Six-fold.
Padding
3 px
Optical breathing room.

Currentcolor. Inherits context.

Below: use monogram only.

VII Chapter Seven · Surface Digital · Voices · Scrim · Lockup · Language · Authority 07 / 09
VII

A surface you
move through.

Print is looked at. A screen is operated. The digital surface is now the largest place this brand is experienced, and the only one where the system has to hold while somebody is using it. Everything here is a rule the other six chapters already implied.

07·01 · Type
There are four voices, not three.

Display, caption and body carry the system. A fourth voice carries the person. It is a hand, and it appears only where somebody greets you or signs their name.

Display
Cormorant Garamond
Titles, ledes, the editorial register.
Caption
IBM Plex Mono
All running metadata, labels and controls.
Body
Inter
Interface prose. Never a headline.
Hand
Playwrite · Meddon
A greeting. A signature. Nothing else, ever.
07·01 The hand is the only voice that is allowed to be irregular. That is why it is rationed. Four voices
07·02 · Photography on screen
Never a veil. Only pools.

Type over a photograph needs protection. A flat wash across the whole frame is not protection, it is a different photograph. Darken only where the words are, and let the darkening fall to nothing everywhere else.

07·02
Localized
Permitted Two pools at most. Each falls to zero.
07·03
Uniform
Rejected A flat veil. It changes the photograph.
07·04 · Lockup
The mark is never recoloured.

On a screen the lockup takes one of two states and no others: the system's negro on a pale ground, the system's crema on a dark one. Anything past that is a tint, and a tinted mark is somebody else's mark.

Desktop
56 px
Max width 360.
Short window
50 px
At 800 high.
Shorter
44 px
At 680 high.
Tablet
46 px
At 1024 wide.
Mobile
40 px
At 720 wide.
07·04 Height is read first, width second, so a short window and a narrow one can never contradict each other. The head grows with the mark. Five steps
07·05 · Language
The brand is bilingual. A person's words are not.

Every surface ships in English and Spanish at exact parity. The switch changes the interface and anything the studio wrote. It never touches a sentence somebody typed themselves.

Parity
1 : 1
Every string carries both. Verified by count, not by eye.
Studio copy
Swaps
Chrome, labels, controls, letters written by us.
Their words
Never
Held exactly as entered. Placement may move. Text may not.
07·05 Translating something a person wrote is the one failure this system cannot recover from. It is not a preference. It is the line. Locked
07·06 · Authority
Which document decides.

Products written on top of this system carry their own specifications. When the two disagree, the boundary below settles it, so the next contradiction resolves itself instead of waiting for someone.

This document governs
The brand
Mark and construction. Palette. The four voices. Photographic devices and scrim. Print. Feed. Anything about how the brand looks.
A product spec governs
The behaviour
Sequence, states, orientation, custody of what a person writes. Anything about how a surface behaves while it is being used.
07·06 A rule about appearance belongs here even when it was discovered while building a product. A rule about behaviour belongs there even when it has a visible result. The boundary

VIII Chapter Eight · Album Wedding Album System · Cover · Layouts · Rhythm · Colophon 08 / 09
VIII

A monograph,
not a photo book.

A carefully held record of the day, edited with intimacy, restraint and intention. The album should never look wedding themed: it is a private photographic monograph made for one couple. The photographs create the emotion. The sequence creates the memory. The system gives the object authorship.

What leads.

Sharnay is recognized through the edit, the pacing, the proportion and the physical details, not because her logo appears fifteen times. The brand never competes with the couple.

01The photographsAlways first
02The emotional sequenceThe memory
03Negative space & compositionThe breath
04Names, date, locationThe record
05Sharnay's signature elementsQuiet, last
08·01 This is the album version of the Encuadre: deciding what leads, what supports it and what should remain quiet. Hierarchy
A · The hero Full spread · emotional peaks · ceremony · kiss · final image
B · Hero plus supporting Place & detail · preparation · encounter · ceremony sequences
C · The editorial three Objects · preparation · vows · family & community
D · The quiet diptych Unequal scale · intimate portraits · transitions · closing rhythm
Brandon & Nicole · MMXXVI

08·02 Five layout families, one controlled vocabulary. The book uses this small family of compositions, not thirty unrelated ones. Faces, hands, the dress and important gestures stay clear of the center fold. Layout families

The rhythm is the brand.

Density, pause, intimacy, scale, pause. Adjacent spreads never repeat the same layout. No more than three photographs on most spreads: four may appear once, and only as a true sequence.

■ Hero · 4–5 ▪▪ Two-image · 5–6 ▪▪▪ Three-image · 3–4 ● Opening / Closing · 1 + 1
08·03 Album-wide rhythm for a fifteen-spread book. The alternation is part of the system, not an afterthought. 15 spreads

The photography stays intact.

Erika's finished photography is the finished work. A photograph may be cropped only to improve the composition while preserving the emotional action.

Never
Filters
No automatic filters. No added sepia. No global black-and-white conversion. No artificial grain.
Never
Effects
No drop shadows. No rounded photo corners. No borders unless one spread uses a deliberate fine-line frame.
Never
Distortion
No stretching. No aggressive crops merely to fit a template.
Always
The fold

IX Chapter Nine · The House Mark · Lockup · Programs · Folio · Signature 09 / 09
IX

One house,
three programs.

The album closes with a signature: photographed by Sharnay Photography. This chapter answers what that signature is and what else it signs. One mark, never two. A single lockup pattern where only the second line changes. And the bindery that serves them all.

09·01Gold on black. Covers, foil, dark surfaces, the Instagram avatar.Primary
09·02Gold on cream. Application headers and light editorial surfaces.Interface
09·03Ink on ivory. Documents, interiors, the album colophon.Print
One mark
The aperture
Solid, complete, gold. The house has one mark and no second symbol competes with it. Programs are distinguished by name, never by a mark of their own.
Clear space
Half its height
On every side. Nothing enters it: no text, no rule, no photograph edge.
Never
A second mark
No program logotype, no monogram, no ring device. This was tested and retired: a symbol that only works in one program's name cannot carry a family.
Sharnay Photography Weddings
Line one
IBM Plex Mono
SHARNAY PHOTOGRAPHY · 9.5 px · tracking 0.3em · uppercase · soft ink. The house speaks in a structural voice.
Line two
Cormorant Garamond
The program name at roughly 2.8 times line one. The program speaks in an editorial voice. This is the only line that changes.
Divider
1 px
Full height of the lockup, ink at 14 percent. It separates mark from name without enclosing either.
Never translated
Proper nouns
Sharnay Photography, Weddings, Bridal, Folio. Retratos is already Spanish and stays. Everything else in an interface translates.
09·04Aperture, pipe, two voices. This pattern is the entire identity system.The lockup

09·05Three programs that read as siblings because they share a structure, not a trick. The system scales: a fourth program enters without debate.The family

Folio sits beside, not below.

A wedding album contains bridal work. A bridal folio may stand alone. The book is precisely where the moments converge, so the bindery cannot belong to any one program. Folio is infrastructure of the house, and the house signs it directly.
